assumptions: Costs are relative: a false reject costs 1 and an escaped defect costs r. r = 20 is an assumption, not a measured plant figure; the sensitivity table shows r = 5 to 100.
Validation and test are 50/50 halves of the official test split; each half holds only dozens of images per class, so intervals are wide and the threshold is noisy.

The test halves are two thirds anomalous (VisA's official test mix), far above a plant's defect rate. False reject rate and escape rate are per class and transfer; cost per 1000 images and the cost-optimal threshold do not, and at a real defect rate the cost would be dominated by false rejects.
Images are VisA product photos, not images from the plant; their link to a line is simulated elsewhere in this project and labelled.
The review band assumes a reviewer decides every image in it correctly and ignores review effort.

published.source: CCAD: Compressed Global Feature Conditioned Anomaly Detection

published.metrics: image AUROC and pixel AUROC (AUPRO is not reported there)
published.setup: Third-party re-run of PatchCore using an LDM (AutoEncoderKL) encoder, 256 x 256 input and a 1000-sample memory bank (the paper's Table 22). Ours: wide_resnet50_2 IMAGENET1K_V1, resize 256, centre crop 224, layers 2 and 3, coreset up to 10% or 16,384 patches. Backbone, crop and coreset differ, so this is a loose reference, not a like for like comparison. Several of its figures (macaroni2 image AUROC 0.472) look weak against other PatchCore reports, which I could not verify from a fetched table.
published.note: The VisA paper (arXiv 2207.14315) does not report PatchCore, so no AUPRO figure for PatchCore on VisA was found in a source I could fetch and read.
